Third-party license for script_tinymce.js
========================================

Component
---------

    TinyMCE, the self-hosted editor build the tinymce_editor mod loads.

    Version:  5.10.7 (2022-12-06)
    Upstream: https://github.com/tinymce/tinymce  (commercial licensing: https://www.tiny.cloud/)
    File:     ./script_tinymce.js  (a verbatim copy of the upstream tinymce.min.js)

Copyright
---------

The banner at the head of script_tinymce.js states, verbatim:

    Copyright (c) Tiny Technologies, Inc. All rights reserved.
    Licensed under the LGPL or a commercial license.
    For LGPL see License.txt in the project root for license information.
    For commercial licenses see https://www.tiny.cloud/
    Version: 5.10.7 (2022-12-06)

License
-------

Dual-licensed: the GNU Lesser General Public License version 2.1, **or** a
Tiny commercial license. This copy is redistributed under the LGPL-2.1 arm.

The banner points the reader at "License.txt in the project root", and the
vendored copy shipped without one. The full text the banner asks for is
therefore shipped here under exactly that name, `./License.txt`; the license
body itself is kept separately as `./License-lgpl-2.1.txt` so the terms are
readable without this note. `License-lgpl-2.1.txt` is the standard GNU LGPL
version 2.1 text (504 lines: preamble, TERMS AND CONDITIONS, END OF TERMS
AND CONDITIONS, and the "How to apply these terms to your new libraries"
appendix), copied verbatim out of a locally vendored TinyMCE distribution
rather than fetched from upstream while this file was written.

What LGPL-2.1 obliges a recipient to do
---------------------------------------

  - Keep this notice and the license text with any redistribution.
  - Make the library's source available. LGPL-2.1 section 6 requires the
    complete corresponding source of the library, or a written offer to
    supply it, to accompany a redistributed binary. The upstream project is
    at https://github.com/tinymce/tinymce.
  - LGPL-2.1's terms are satisfiable inside this project: the surrounding
    engine is GPL-3.0-or-later, whose section 6 is the GPL's copy-and-modify
    mechanism. See NOTICE at the repository root for the derivative-work
    scope.

The commercial alternative
--------------------------

The same component is available from Tiny under a commercial license at
https://www.tiny.cloud/. Choosing that arm is a licensing decision for
whoever redistributes this package, not a code change: the vendored bytes
are identical either way.
